screening_results.reason: This is a task-based fMRI study of complex arithmetic in healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and BOLD fMRI results (meets I5, I6, I8). However, the provided full text does not include stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI coordinate listings for the reported activation peaks, and there is no clear presentation of voxelwise coordinates in the supplied content (does not meet I7). The text also does not provide coordinate results in tables/figures or indicate their availability in supplementary material within the provided file (does not meet I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore I must exclude the study because not all required inclusion criteria (I7 and I9) are satisfied in the supplied full text.

Although this article is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults with whole-brain analyses, stereotactic coordinates reported, and BOLD analyses (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), it does not meet the required definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The in-scanner task is a three-back working-memory/interference task (lure vs non-lure trials), which probes attentional control and working memory rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm as defined (involving evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions and executing operations to arrive at a novel solution). The Raven’s Progressive Matrices (a problem-solving measure) was administered outside the scanner and was not the task used during neuroimaging, so the neural data do not reflect task-based problem solving across domains. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

The study uses a paced visual serial addition task (PVSAT/PASAT) which requires applying an arithmetic rule to compute consecutive sums (goal-directed, rule-conforming operations involving working memory and executive control), meeting the review’s definition of problem-solving. It reports a whole-brain, random-effects group analysis in healthy adult participants (n=9), uses task-based BOLD fMRI, and presents stereotactic coordinates referenced to Talairach space in tables/figures. Voxelwise results are provided in group-level tables and figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Caveat: the task is a highly constrained arithmetic/attention task rather than open-ended problem solving, but it satisfies the inclusion criteria as defined.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation using an abstract reasoning task that requires identifying the next item in a sequence (goal-directed problem solving via pattern detection, planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a correct response), meeting the review’s operational definition of problem solving. It includes whole-brain, group-level analyses for both alcohol-dependent and healthy adult control groups (one-sample t tests and between-group tests), reports BOLD results, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-empirical, or absence of healthy-group task effects) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that investigates relational reasoning—a logical problem-solving task requiring goal-directed inference and manipulation of relations (meets the review definition of problem solving). The study reports group-level, whole-brain analyses using SPM with cluster-level correction, provides stereotactic coordinates referenced to Talairach space, and uses BOLD EPI fMRI. Voxelwise/task-related activation results are described across the whole brain (conjunctions and contrasts) with coordinates and cluster descriptions. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using the Raven's Progressive Matrices (a well-established problem-solving/fluid-reasoning task), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=79). Whole-brain analyses were performed (group ICA, within-subject ANOVA) with group-level effects reported. The study uses BOLD fMRI. Stereotactic locations and cluster peaks are indicated (MNI standard space is referenced and Supplementary Table I is described as providing voxel locations for RPM–rest contrasts), satisfying coordinate reporting and acceptable placement in supplementary materials. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental coordinate tables are referenced. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that explicitly required subjects to determine the next best chess move (a goal-directed problem-solving task). The study reports a group-level, whole-brain fixed-effects analysis (spatial normalization to Talairach space) with voxelwise activation results and Talairach coordinates provided. BOLD T2*-weighted EPI was used to measure activation. Voxelwise results are reported in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants performing complex multiplication problems that require goal-directed calculation and rule-based operations (meets I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI (I8). Voxelwise results and statistical maps/tables are reported (I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (E3–E6 not met). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion as a whole-brain task-based fMRI investigation of problem-solving in healthy adults.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. Although it uses task-based fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with stereotactic coordinates (meeting I6, I7, I8, and I9), the experimental paradigm is route learning/spatial navigation and memory (encoding and retrieval of temporo-spatial landmark associations), not a domain-general problem-solving task as defined by I5 (i.e., a goal-directed need to figure out a method, involving critical evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions or rule-based operations to reach a novel solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using Raven's Standard Progressive Matrices (matrix reasoning), which meets the review definition of problem solving. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM) with task-related BOLD contrasts and tables/figures of stereotactic coordinates in MNI space. Healthy non-autistic adult control participants are included and their within-group task effects are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=10) using mental arithmetic (subtraction and multiplication), which constitutes a problem-solving task under rule-based operations (arithmetic procedures and retrieval). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (FWE-corrected cluster-level threshold) and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (e.g., left hIPS x=−37,y=−48,z=49 and right hIPS x=44,y=−45,z=54). BOLD fMRI was used and task-related activations are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based problem-solving), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (coordinates/results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusion).

The task (three-operand arithmetic) fits the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed operation using rule-based computations) and the study used whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses with BOLD (I5, I6, I8 met). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) or indicate that coordinate tables/figures/supplementary materials with coordinates are available, so it fails inclusion criterion I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I7). Full text appears complete for purposes of screening (no indication that coordinate tables were omitted).

This study reports task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants performing calculation tasks that involve rule-based operations (exact and approximate arithmetic), which fit the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed operations using algebraic/semantic rules to arrive at correct/approximate solutions). The paper includes group-level adult task effects (within-group math > control contrasts), reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space, and presents BOLD results. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for this review.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates. However, the experimental tasks are nonsymbolic numerical, spatial orientation, and color discriminations (magnitude/comparison and perceptual decision tasks), not problem-solving tasks as defined by the review (i.e., requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at novel solutions). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 do not apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of verbal insight (chengyu) riddles in healthy adults, with event-related whole-brain GLM (random-effects) analyses and reported stereotactic peak coordinates. The task operationalizes problem solving by requiring participants to select a novel, reasonable answer (goal-directed solution selection involving constraint relaxation and representation change). Whole-brain activation contrasts (insight vs. rest, noninsight vs. rest, insight vs. noninsight) were performed and thresholded, group-level effects are reported, and peak coordinates are provided (via SPM preprocessing/normalization). Functional connectivity and ROI time-series were secondary but do not replace the whole-brain results. Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9; no exclusion criteria apply. No substantive missing core sections detected; full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using the Wason selection task (deductive/problem-solving). The task meets the review's problem-solving definition (goal-driven selection of cards to detect rule violations; requires logical evaluation, planning/strategy, and rule-constrained operations). Methods report whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (second-level paired t tests and conjunctions), voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and BOLD fMRI acquisition/analyses. Results include coordinate-based activation tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using Raven Progressive Matrices (analytic and figural) — a well-defined problem-solving task requiring identification of rules and applying operations to derive solutions. The authors performed whole-brain random-effects voxel-wise analyses at the group level (N=18), reporting activations transformed into Talairach space and presenting significant cluster coordinates (Table I and figures). BOLD signal (percent signal change) analyses and ANOVAs are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided content is complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I5–I9) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task (meets I5) and reports BOLD signal analyses (meets I8). However, the imaging analysis used individually delineated VOIs and reported percentage activation within those VOIs rather than a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis in a normalized stereotactic space. The authors explicitly avoided normalization and did not report Talairach/MNI coordinates or voxelwise whole-brain tables/figures. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults) and I7 (stereotactic coordinate results) are not met. This also triggers exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7, (and I9 not satisfied). Exclusion criteria met: E3. Consequently the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in the meta-analysis objective. It is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study of Theory of Mind (ToM) using animated shapes and contrasts ToM versus random motion; the task does not involve goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations, or rule-based solution execution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (includes whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported/tabled). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (does NOT study a problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3, E4, E5, or E6). Full text appears complete. Because I5 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of geometric analogical problem solving in healthy adults (mean age 18.7). The task requires goal-directed problem solving (identifying and mapping relations to reach a correct judgment) meeting the review's problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level mixed-effects analyses (FLAME) with cluster thresholds, BOLD-based fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates for activated regions (e.g., RLPFC coordinates), and presents voxelwise results in figures/tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. The tactile multiple T-maze is a goal-directed task requiring planning/sequencing and rule-based navigation (meets I5). The paper reports task-based BOLD fMRI with group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adult participants (congenitally blind and blindfolded sighted controls) (meets I6 and I8). Results are reported with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and coordinate tables/figures (meets I7 and I9). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, and analyses include whole-brain contrasts and group comparisons rather than ROI-only results. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates learning and execution of algorithmic arithmetic problems (strategy vs. drill), which fits the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed, planning/sequencing operations, rule-based execution). The study used whole-brain BOLD fMRI with group-level contrasts (fixed-effects analysis across nine healthy adults), reports stereotactic coordinates transformed to Talairach space in tables, and presents voxelwise task-related activation results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient-only, empirical with healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

The study uses a probabilistic reversal learning task (reinforcement learning) and analyzes ventral striatal prediction error signals. While it meets several technical imaging criteria (group-level whole-brain GLM, stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD analyses), the task does not fit the meta-analysis definition of a 'problem solving' task (goal-directed complex planning, sequencing operations, or critical-thinking to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI results) are strictly triggered, as a whole-brain GLM was performed (though main inferences used SVC in VS). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of four-term analogical reasoning (a problem-solving task requiring goal-directed inference and mapping). It recruited healthy adult participants (n=20) and performed group-level SPM analyses on BOLD data with whole-brain coverage. The paper reports stereotactic (MNI) activation coordinates (including RLPFC peaks) and task-related increases; voxelwise results and coordinates are presented. Although ROI analyses were used to characterize PFC effects, the study conducted whole-brain GLM preprocessing and group analyses and reports coordinate results. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of the Tower of London problem-solving task in healthy adults (n=22). The study performed whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) with FWE correction after normalization to MNI space, reporting task-related activations; BOLD EPI data were acquired and analyzed. Although an ROI approach was used for some analyses, whole-brain voxelwise results were explicitly reported and used to define ROIs, so the study is not ROI-only. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based problem-solving), I6 (whole-brain group effects in healthy adults), I7 (MNI stereotactic normalization/coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation using the Raven's Progressive Matrices, a problem-solving/analogical reasoning task (meets I5). It includes a healthy adult control group and reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps for the control (NC) group and combined analyses (meets I6). Analyses were performed in MNI space and peak coordinates/locations are reported (meets I7). The study uses BOLD fMRI with voxelwise whole-brain results (meets I8). Task-related voxelwise results are reported in main text/figures and are available as stereotactic results (meets I9). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not solely disease/age/gender comparisons (E4), include healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts (E5), and it is empirical original data (not E6). Therefore the article should be INCLUDED.

The study is a task-based BOLD fMRI investigation in healthy adult surgery residents performing a mental rotation task, with whole-brain, group-level contrasts and regression analyses reported (meets I5, I6, I8). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations—results are described by Brodmann areas, cluster statistics, and figures but no coordinate tables or explicit standardized-space coordinates are present in the supplied content. Because I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates) is not satisfied, the study cannot be included per the review criteria. Full text appears complete for intro/methods/results/discussion (no supplementary coordinate tables provided).

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants solving arithmetic word problems (a goal-directed problem-solving task). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (multiple regression), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and presents BOLD task-related activation results (tables/figures). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task definition (I5), whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic coordinates reported (I7), BOLD/fMRI analysis (I8), and availability of voxelwise results in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and includes healthy-group task effects).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a mental calculation task (subtractions/additions/multiplications) that meets the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed operations following rules to reach correct solutions). The study reports whole-brain random effects analyses with voxelwise results and peak coordinates in standardized space (MNI), presents BOLD fMRI contrasts (calculation vs control), and provides group-level effects. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study includes a task that meets the review’s definition of problem solving (a deductive logic localizer where participants judged validity of arguments), reports group-level whole-brain analyses, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach-normalized) in tables and text. The paper contains full methods, results (including whole-brain and ROI analyses derived from the logic localizer), and discussion in healthy adult participants. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses an n-back working memory task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed multi-step problem solving, planning/sequencing to reach a previously unknown solution). Therefore it fails I5. It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults reported) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). The provided full text does not explicitly report stereotactic peak coordinates in Talairach or MNI space in the excerpt (so I7 is not clearly met from the provided manuscript). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I5 (problem-solving task) is not met; possibly I7 also not demonstrably met in the provided text.

This is a task-based, event-related fMRI study in healthy adults that used an arithmetic verification task (determine whether presented equations are correct), which meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed evaluation and execution of rule-based arithmetic operations). The study reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses across 16 healthy adult subjects using stereotaxic Talairach normalization, BOLD fMRI acquisition and analysis (T2*-weighted images, SPM99), and presents activation foci (coordinates/figures/tables). Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core content appears complete.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adult participants performing arithmetic (multiplication) verification, which qualifies as a problem-solving task (goal-directed operations to arrive at correct solutions). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM5, provides stereotactic (MNI) coordinates for task-related activation (e.g., left angular gyrus peak), and uses BOLD fMRI. Coordinate and voxelwise results are reported and validated with regression and ROI follow-ups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all included criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a goal-directed virtual navigation task that required learning object locations and planning routes (meets the review’s problem-solving definition, I5). The study performed voxel-wise, whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adult participants (I6) using BOLD fMRI (I8). The manuscript reports standardized stereotactic activation results (BA clusters and references to cluster coordinates/figures/tables), satisfying I7 and I9. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (core content present). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects in healthy adults).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20) that used arithmetic tasks (exact and approximate calculation, magnitude comparison). These tasks involve goal-directed, rule-based problem solving (selecting/calculating correct sums or magnitude comparisons) and thus meet the review's problem-solving definition. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise BOLD analyses (SPM99) with FWE/FDR correction and between- and within-group statistical maps; stereotactic coordinates are given (MNI transformed to Talairach). Group-level effects for healthy adults are reported. Full-text includes methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy adult task effects). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This task-based fMRI study uses the PASAT, a rule-based, goal-directed arithmetic task involving planning/sequencing and execution (meets problem-solving definition). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses for healthy control participants, provides stereotactic Talairach x,y,z coordinates, and uses BOLD-fMRI (all satisfying I5–I9). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of problem-solving in healthy adults.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=28) using a maze navigation task that meets the review definition of problem solving (clear goal: reach maze end; planning/sequencing and execution of actions). The authors report group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects, contrasts across participants), BOLD fMRI methods, and state stereotactic coordinate results (coordinates/figures referenced). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using the Beauty Contest game, which requires a clear goal (win the prize) and rule-based strategic reasoning/planning (iterated best-reply, mental calculation, and action selection) consistent with the review's definition of problem solving. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random effects analyses in 20 healthy adults, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for activations (e.g., mPFC, TPJ), and uses BOLD fMRI measures. Coordinates and contrasts are reported in the main text and supplementary materials. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes within-healthy-group task effects). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=32) that used a two-digit arithmetic verification task requiring procedural calculation and judgment—meeting the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed calculation using rule-based operations). The study reports group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (SPM5; voxel-wise t-statistics, p<0.001) and BOLD fMRI acquisition. The manuscript indicates voxelwise cluster results and refers to figures/tables for activation loci (conjunction, direct, and interaction contrasts), consistent with stereotactic reporting conventions (coordinates implied in results/tables/figures). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore I5, I6, I8 and I9 are satisfied, and I7 is considered satisfied based on the main text indicating voxelwise stereotactic results available in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports a task-based BOLD fMRI experiment in healthy adults using a virtual maze navigation task that requires participants to form an allocentric ‘cognitive map’ and select the correct map (goal-directed behavior requiring translation/representation and selection), which meets the problem-solving definition (goal + need to determine a way to reach it and execute an action to select the correct map). The paper includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, reports stereotactic coordinates, and provides ROI analyses in addition to voxelwise results. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that employed reasoning and episodic-memory-based reasoning tasks (meets I5), performed group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (meets I6), and reports BOLD-based fMRI results (meets I8). However, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate results in either Talairach or MNI space (no coordinate tables or coordinate figures are shown in the supplied content), so inclusion criterion I7 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because not all required inclusion criteria are met (missing I7).

This study is an fMRI investigation of moral reasoning comparing ASD patients and healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (reports whole-brain group-level analyses including healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (task-related BOLD fMRI results), I9 (voxelwise results are presented in tables/figures/supplement). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the task is moral decision-making/dilemma evaluation rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review, which requires goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing operations within defined rule sets—semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical, etc.). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not examine a problem-solving task per the review’s I5 definition.

The study includes a task (mental arithmetic) that meets the review's problem-solving definition: participants have a goal (add presented numbers and choose the correct sum) and must perform rule-based operations (arithmetic) to reach a correct solution. It is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (meditators and controls), with group-level random-effects analyses and whole-brain exploratory analyses reported. Stereotactic coordinates are provided in MNI space, and the imaging modality is task BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are reported (tables/coordinates and text). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Although the arithmetic task was used as a control for a meditation study, the task nonetheless qualifies as a problem-solving task for the meta-analysis objective. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that administered arithmetic problem-solving (addition and subtraction) and an order-judgment task. It includes whole-brain group-level analyses (GLM and searchlight AVC) on 17 healthy adults, reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for task-related activations, and uses BOLD fMRI. Results are presented with coordinates and statistical thresholds. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This empirical fMRI study includes a mental calculation task (silent subtraction) that meets the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed numerical operations following rule-based arithmetic). It reports whole-brain voxelwise random-effects group analyses on 81 healthy adult subjects, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for task-related activations, and uses BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are presented in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the study investigates autobiographical memory and self-reflection (remembering content vs reflecting on meaning) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the meta-analysis (I5 not met). The study does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic/MNI coordinates), I8 (task-related BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD-fMRI study of numerical inductive reasoning, which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (identifying a rule from a number series and generating the next number). The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (within-group task vs rest and between-group comparisons) using SPM8, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (figures and supplementary tables), and uses BOLD-fMRI. Participants were healthy adult groups (young and elderly) screened for cognitive impairment. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a whole-brain, task-based BOLD fMRI study that includes healthy adult controls and reports group-level within-group effects and stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for task-related activations. The task (PASAT) requires subjects to maintain and manipulate numerical information and perform arithmetic additions following a rule set, which fits the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (operations conforming to an algebraic/arithmetic rule set). Voxelwise whole-brain analyses and coordinate results are reported in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using social and mechanical reasoning tasks that require goal-directed inference and problem solving (physics puzzles and false-belief/social inference questions). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (random- and fixed-effects) on 45 healthy adults, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic peak coordinates (711-2B/Talairach-space) and voxelwise results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based PET study of the Tower of London problem-solving task (meets I5). It includes healthy adult controls with group-level task effects and whole-brain analyses (I6). This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using a multiplication verification task that requires goal-directed calculation, sequencing and execution of arithmetic operations (meets I5). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses in Talairach space with cluster-level correction and provides stereotactic/ROI coordinates (meets I6 and I7). It uses BOLD fMRI (meets I8) and voxelwise results are available in tables/figures (meets I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered: the study is not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and includes healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided content, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in stereotactic (Talairach) space (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied), the experimental task is simple arithmetic fact retrieval (multiplication verification) aimed at retrieval of stored solutions rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires planning, sequencing actions, or generating novel solutions. The review’s I5 defines problem solving as involving evaluation/planning/sequencing operations to reach a goal; this study focuses on memory retrieval of learned facts and rehearsal effects, not on solving new or structured problems. Therefore I5 is not met, and the study should be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of empathic reasoning about facial expressions, not a problem-solving task as defined by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results described in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the task requires selecting which of four situational sentences best matches an observed facial expression (social/emotional inference), but does not involve problem-solving as defined (goal-directed planning, sequencing operations or applying rule-based procedures to arrive at a novel solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded because it fails I5 (problem-solving task requirement).

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of mental calculation (arithmetic operations) in healthy adults. Mental calculation meets the review's problem-solving definition (rule-based operations to reach a correct solution). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise BOLD analyses using a second-level random-effects model, conjunction and contrast maps, and reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI→Talairach). Voxelwise results and thresholds are described and coordinates are indicated in the text/tables/figures. The sample comprises healthy adult participants. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in adults using a goal-directed wayfinding task that requires planning/sequencing to find the shortest route (meets I5). The paper includes healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain analyses (within-group and between-group effects) (meets I6). Images were normalized to ICBM templates and SPM analyses were conducted; the manuscript references result tables/figures for reported activations (indicating stereotactic reporting in standardized space per I7 and allowed under I9). BOLD (fMRI) analyses are explicitly reported (meets I8). The study is not ROI-only and includes whole-brain results and healthy-group task effects, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and appears complete. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for this review and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (a problem-solving task) including five healthy adult controls and whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The authors registered results to MNI standard space, report BOLD (blood oxygen–dependent) analyses, and present voxelwise activation results in figures/tables. The study reports group-level activation maps for the normal control group (random-effects mean maps) and contrasts versus the patient. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion; not truncated.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that used a conditional/logical reasoning task requiring participants to apply logical rules (problem-solving within a logical framework). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (SPM8), with voxelwise results and peak coordinates (MNI normalization) and BOLD-based fMRI contrasts (e.g., LC vs BC) reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain neuroimaging studies of problem solving.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults investigating problem-solving (complex multiplication and figural-spatial problems). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise MNI coordinates (FWE-corrected) and BOLD fMRI measures. Tasks meet the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed problem solving with rule-based operations and execution). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study is task-based fMRI of a planning/problem-solving task (Tower of London) in healthy adults with group-level random-effects analysis and reports BOLD results; however, the provided full text does not include stereotactic (Talairach or MNI) coordinates for task-related activations. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no coordinates reported in provided text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete but lacks explicit coordinate tables or numerical stereotactic results required for inclusion.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants that investigates goal-directed navigation requiring participants to plan and select sequences of actions to reach maze goals. The task meets the review's operational definition of problem solving (goal-directed behavior, planning/sequencing, rule-based choices). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and BOLD fMRI results (multiple whole-brain tables/figures). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full article text (methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London planning/problem-solving paradigm (meets I5). It includes healthy adult control participants and reports group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses comparing controls and HD groups (meets I6). Analyses are BOLD-based (meets I8). Data were spatially normalized to MNI space, a seed coordinate in MNI is reported (MNI −4/54/−8), and the manuscript describes voxelwise cluster results and refers to cluster/figure information (satisfies I7 and I9 given that stereotactic results are presented in MNI space and cluster results are indicated in the paper/figures). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study (with concurrent EEG) of a problem-solving task (Chinese character chunk decomposition) in healthy adult participants. It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects fMRI analyses using BOLD contrast, presents voxelwise stereotactic coordinates (MNI converted to Talairach) and cluster results, and provides behavioral and imaging results across conditions. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, procedure, fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical-group comparisons, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study of deductive reasoning (conditional and syllogistic problems) in healthy adults (n=26). The tasks require goal-directed, rule-based problem solving (logical integration to derive conclusions), meeting the review’s problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM2, BOLD (fMRI) results, and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures and supplementary maps). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I9). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mathematical problem solving in healthy adult participants (N=20 university students). It reports group-level BOLD analyses, whole-brain classification (MVPA) and an exploratory whole-brain contrast with cluster tables referenced, and provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach coordinates reported for angular gyrus and HIPS coordinates used). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based problem-solving fMRI), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analyses), and I9 (voxelwise/coordinate results available in tables/figures). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study directly addresses task-based functional neuroimaging of problem solving using the Tower of London (a prototypical planning/problem-solving task requiring a goal and sequencing of moves). It reports both fMRI (BOLD) and PET (rCBF) analyses, with group-level voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses in healthy adult participants. The methods state transformation to stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) and reporting of coordinate-based statistical parametric maps; results describe task-related increases in specific brain regions (Brodmann areas) and thresholds, consistent with coordinate-based reporting. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a patient-group-only or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London problem-solving paradigm (meets I5). Participants were healthy adults (N=24) and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (meets I6). Functional images were normalized to MNI space and stereotactic peak coordinates/VOI peak coordinates are described and referenced (meets I7 and I9). The study used BOLD fMRI (3T EPI) and reports task-related hemodynamic effects (meets I8). Analyses include voxelwise whole-brain results (with thresholds and cluster extents) and are not limited to ROI-only findings. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an algebraic problem-solving task in which participants perform goal-directed problem solving), I6 (group-level, whole-brain coverage via 408 ROIs and group classifier analyses on healthy adults), and I8 (BOLD fMRI percent-change analyses). The study reports a task (virtual Morris Water Task) that meets the review's problem-solving definition: subjects have a clear goal (find the platform) and must plan and execute navigation/search strategies to reach it. It uses task-based fMRI with whole-brain analyses (ICA and GLM) and reports group-level effects including healthy adult controls. Results are presented in standardized MNI space and include BOLD signal analyses and voxelwise results (ICA components, GLM contrasts, VBM associations), satisfying reporting requirements. The full-text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI results, is empirical with original human data, and includes healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (two experiments with N=16 and N=21, ages 20–40) that investigates nonverbal problem solving (rule derivation and application), meeting the meta-analysis definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses (SPM5) with FDR-corrected maps, peak stereotactic coordinates (MNI), and BOLD-based contrasts for task effects and experimental manipulations. Results include whole-brain maps, coordinate tables, and ROI backup analyses. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, not a review, includes within-group task activations). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core article content appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that uses arithmetic (exact and approximate calculation) tasks which constitute rule-based problem-solving (goal-directed operations to compute or estimate sums). The study reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses using SPM, provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI), and presents voxelwise results in tables/figures. Therefore it satisfies I5 (task meets problem-solving definition via algebraic/arithmetic operations), I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (results available in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/references).

Full text shows an fMRI BOLD study of a probabilistic decision/inference (Jumping-to-Conclusions) task in healthy adults, but analyses were conducted on predefined ROIs (Harvard-Oxford masks) and the paper does not present whole-brain, voxelwise, stereotactic-coordinate group-level results required for this review. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (reports BOLD analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not clearly match the review's definition of problem-solving across domains), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis reported), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate results given in main text or supplements). Exclusion criterion met: E3 (reports only ROI results). Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results with stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The experimental tasks are number-line estimation and brightness estimation (mapping magnitudes to spatial positions), which are estimation/psychophysical tasks rather than goal-directed problem-solving requiring planning, sequencing, or execution of operations to reach an unknown solution. Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables), so exclusion is based on ineligible task content rather than incomplete reporting or other exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of algebra problem solving in healthy adult participants (N=20). It reports BOLD analyses and group-level task effects, conducts exploratory whole-brain analyses with reported Talairach coordinates for multiple regions (predefined ROIs and additional clusters), and presents task-related increases in brain activity. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review: I5 (task-based problem-solving task—algebra), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, modeling, and conclusions and appears complete. Hence INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI empirical study of fluid-reasoning/problem-solving tasks (Induction and Visualization) in healthy adult participants (N=22, ages 20–24). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not merely abstract/metadata). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied.

While this is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates, the experimental tasks are virtual navigation and memory/strategy learning (4/8VM and CSDLT) assessing hippocampus vs caudate-dependent spatial vs response strategies. These tasks probe memory and navigational strategy selection rather than problem-solving as defined for the meta-analysis (i.e., tasks requiring goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing operations within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical or similar rule-based frameworks to arrive at a novel solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. The manuscript otherwise meets I6, I7, I8 (and I9 as coordinates/results are reported), and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (BOLD) in healthy adult participants (N=14) using the Wason Selection Task, a logical deductive/problem-solving task that requires identifying/testing rule violations (fits problem-solving definition involving goal, evaluation, and rule-based operations). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and corrected thresholds, and also provides ROI analyses and stereotactic coordinates. Thus it meets I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, includes healthy-group task effects, and reports whole-brain results rather than only ROIs. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study uses a virtual navigation (T-maze) task and reports whole-brain BOLD group analyses with MNI coordinates in healthy adults, so it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the experimental task is spatial navigation with simple left/right choices for reward (with feedback determined randomly) and auxiliary assessments of spatial ability. It does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or executing operations within a rule-based framework to derive solutions. Therefore I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related, task-based whole-brain fMRI study of healthy adult participants performing Wason selection tasks (conditional proposition testing), which constitutes a rule-based logical problem-solving task. The paper reports group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses and BOLD (T2*-weighted EPI) results, with activation contrasts (Falsification vs BL, Non-Falsification vs BL, Falsification vs Non-Falsification, MT vs Non-Falsification, MT vs MP). Images were normalized in SPM2 and thresholded with FDR; the manuscript indicates coordinate/activation tables and supplementary materials are available online, consistent with reporting stereotactic results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient-group-only, not between-group-only, empirical human data). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and should be included.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (ACC and lPFC) analyses and percent signal-change results rather than whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation maps or stereotactic coordinate tables of activation peaks. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of a problem-solving task in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no evidence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (no task-related activation peaks reported as stereotactic coordinates in results/tables—ROI center coordinates are provided but not whole-brain activation coordinates), I9 (no indication that voxelwise results are available in tables/figures/supplement). Exclusion criterion met: E3 (reports only ROI results). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment using the paced visual serial addition task (PVSAT), which involves goal-directed, rule-based arithmetic operations (satisfying the review's broad definition of problem solving). It includes whole-brain, group-level within-group analyses for healthy adult controls (n=18) using SPM with normalization to MNI space and reports stereotactic coordinates (e.g., sphere at x=-2,y=28,z=22). The study uses BOLD fMRI contrasts (calculation > control) and provides voxelwise results in figures/tables. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical human data).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a problem-solving task (trial-and-error search with exploration/exploitation). It reports whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses, BOLD results, and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space. The task meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed search, evaluation, planning/execution to find correct stimulus). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that includes a problem-solving/planning paradigm (Tower of London) meeting the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing). The study performed group-level whole-brain GLM analyses (Test and Repetition samples) with SPM, normalized to MNI space, and reports lists of significant clusters (coordinates) for task contrasts (planning vs baseline). BOLD EPI fMRI was the modality used. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and provides adequate detail for inclusion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level BOLD results in standardized stereotactic space. It therefore satisfies I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the experimental task is a magnitude/lateness comparison (choose larger number or later event) and semantic retrieval of known historic dates, not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (i.e., it does not require setting a goal and devising/planning/executing a sequence of operations to reach a novel or nontrivial solution). The paradigm assesses number/semantic processing and sequencing/ordering judgments rather than evaluation, planning, or executing operations to solve a presented problem. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I5.

This is an fMRI task study of planning (Tower of London and navigation) in healthy adults that reports whole-brain BOLD contrasts and stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates (I5, I7, I8, I9 satisfied). However, it is a single-subject/case study (n=1) and does not include any group-level healthy adult effects; inclusion criterion I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults) is not met. Therefore it does not provide the group-level voxelwise results required for the meta-analysis. Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the study does not include any healthy-group task effect/group-level contrasts. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study uses task-based BOLD imaging in healthy adult participants (n=25) performing an arithmetic equation-verification task and an operation-span (OSPAN) complex span task. The arithmetic condition requires evaluating equations and executing arithmetic operations (semantic/algebraic rule-based processing), which fits the meta-analysis definition of problem-solving (goal-directed evaluation and operation sequencing). The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (warped to MNI space), ROI and whole-brain contrasts (task>baseline; OSPAN>Arithmetic), and provides stereotactic-based results and cluster tables consistent with reporting in MNI coordinates. Thus it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (young female participants) using problem-solving/reasoning tasks (induction, visualization, spatial relationships) that require selecting the correct missing figure — meeting the review's definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level analyses (random effects), BOLD fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach examples and reported peak coordinates). Voxelwise results are presented in maps/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so completeness is sufficient.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates; however, the experimental task is mental rotation/discrimination (judging whether two images are identical or mirror images), which is a visuospatial imagery/discrimination task rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined in I5 (involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or executing operations within a rule set to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Therefore it does not meet I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none ([])

This full text is complete. I exclude because it does not meet I5: the fMRI task was passive viewing of addition expressions with participants instructed to make no responses; although authors infer spontaneous/automatic calculation, participants were not engaged in an explicit problem-solving task (no goal-directed planning, sequencing, or execution to reach a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinate results reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported), and I9 (voxelwise results available in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task does not satisfy the review’s operational definition of a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore I exclude the study from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of planning/problem solving (Tower of London) in healthy adults (N=17). It uses whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM) with random-effects group-level statistics and reports task-related BOLD increases and stereotactic coordinates (MNI→Talairach conversion). A BOLD analysis and parametric contrasts are reported with FWE-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of mental arithmetic (a problem-solving task involving goal-directed calculation and rule-based operations) in 20 healthy adult participants. It includes whole-brain, group-level analyses (second-level SPM), reports BOLD results, and provides stereotactic coordinates for task-related activations (Talairach/MNI-style coordinates) in tables/figures. Voxelwise results are reported and discussed. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results with peak coordinates (MNI) and group-level analyses, but the experimental paradigm is spatial working memory and perspective-taking (allocentric vs egocentric recall), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no explicit goal-directed problem to be solved, planning/sequencing of actions, or executing operations to derive a novel solution). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates for activations (e.g., x=-42,y=26,z=37 and others) consistent with Talairach/MNI reporting (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI analyses (I8). This is a task-based fMRI study of logical reasoning (syllogisms) in healthy adults that fits the review's problem-solving definition—participants must determine whether conclusions follow from premises (logical rule-based problem solving). It reports group-level, whole-brain BOLD analyses using SPM with spatial normalization to the MNI template and voxelwise stereotactic coordinates (e.g., MNI coords provided). Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (meets I6, I8) and reports group-level whole-brain results with stereotactic peak/beta data (figures/supplementary tables imply coordinates; meets I7 and I9), the experimental paradigm is an instrumental visuomotor associative learning / trial-and-error conditioning task. It does not involve the type of problem-solving defined in the review (i.e., tasks requiring critical evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions, or application of explicit rule-based/semantic/algebraic/logical operations to arrive at a novel solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task as defined) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study is an fMRI investigation of mental subtraction in healthy adults and reports group-level activation differences and BOLD EPI data (meets I5 and I8). However, it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis: (1) Whole-brain coverage/analysis (I6) appears not satisfied — imaging used only 10 slices parallel to AC–PC, suggesting limited brain coverage rather than whole-brain analysis; (2) No stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) are reported in the full text (I7); (3) No voxelwise stereotactic coordinates are provided in text/tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I6/I7/I9 are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) and random-effects analyses. The tasks include deductive reasoning (DR) requiring logical inference to determine hat color given constraints, which meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed logical operations). Whole-brain contrasts (e.g., DR vs. PC, MI vs. DR) are reported with cluster-level correction and coordinates; BOLD analyses and voxelwise results are presented. Participants are healthy adults. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the review criteria: participants performed goal-directed, rule-based mental transformations (transposition and reversal) to determine whether a target melody matched a transformed sample, constituting a problem-solving operation as defined in I5. Whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses are reported (I6) with BOLD contrasts (I8). Images/analyses were transformed to MNI/ICBM stereotaxic space and voxelwise results/conjunctions are reported (I7,I9). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is sufficient for extraction. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of reasoning in healthy adults that explicitly requires subjects to deduce and apply a sequencing rule (i.e., problem-solving involving goal-directed planning/sequencing). The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (FDR-corrected) in normalized stereotactic space (MNI305), provides stereotactic results/coordinates (figures/tables referenced), and uses BOLD fMRI. Participants are healthy adults (n=19). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not clinical-group comparisons only, includes within-healthy-group task effects, and is empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a goal-directed virtual navigation/place-learning task that requires subjects to plan/sequence actions to retrieve objects (meets problem-solving definition). It reports group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses (n=14) with statistical maps and tables, provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates for peak activations, and includes voxelwise results in tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a clinical-group-only comparison, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria below are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=21) using game tasks that require problem solving (dominance-solvable games necessitate iterative elimination, planning, and rule-based reasoning), satisfying the definition of problem-solving tasks. The study reports whole-brain, group-level activation contrasts (frontoparietal, insula, ACC) and refers to coordinate tables in the supplementary materials (tables S2, S3, S10–S13), satisfying the requirement that stereotactic coordinates are reported or available. BOLD fMRI was used. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary coordinate tables are referenced (acceptable per I9). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a patient/group-comparison-only study, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD-fMRI study in healthy adults using a visuo-spatial reasoning (VSRT) task that requires goal-directed evaluation and rule verification (problem-solving). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (linear trend contrast of relational complexity), normalization to MNI space, and extraction of ROI coordinates (with results presented in figures/tables/supplement). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. The study is not ROI-only and includes healthy adult participants. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study reports a task-based BOLD fMRI investigation of relational reasoning, a rule-based problem-solving paradigm (assessing relations across dimensions and applying abstract rules), satisfying the review's definition of problem solving (I5). It includes whole-brain, group-level analyses with results reported for age groups including a healthy Adult group (I6), and presents stereotactic coordinates for peak activations (e.g., [−48 45 −3], [3 27 42], [−30 27 0]) and tables/figures (I7, I9). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using a number bisection task that requires goal-directed, rule-based operations (deciding whether the middle number is the correct mean), satisfying the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adult participants (I6), presents stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for task-related effects (I7), and reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8). Voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in the main text (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), the paper reports healthy-group task effects (not only between-group contrasts), and it is an empirical study.
