The analysis is whole-brain (EPI BOLD fMRI) with group-level results reported, Talairach stereotactic coordinates provided for activated ROIs, and task-related increases described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not rely solely on ROI-only reporting. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and the study should be included.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using the Wason selection task (logical/problem-solving task requiring identification of violations and rule-based reasoning). It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and cluster results, and describes BOLD imaging methods and results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based problem-solving fMRI studies (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based PET study of mental calculation (abacus-based contiguous addition), which meets the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed arithmetic operations following rule sets). It reports whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adult participants (abacus experts and non-experts) using SPM2, with rCBF PET data (15O-water). Results are presented in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space with voxelwise activation maps/tables and between- and within-group contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of task design and coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects). Therefore the study satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included.

This is an empirical PET study with 41 healthy adults performing two problem-solving/abstract reasoning tasks (WCST and Raven’s Progressive Matrices), which meet the review’s problem-solving definition. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise SPM analyses (task minus control), provides group-level effects in healthy adults, and reports regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) results with stereotactic normalization to Talairach space and tabulated local maxima/coordinates in tables and figures. Voxelwise results and across-task comparisons are presented. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects beyond age comparisons). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 are satisfied.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates (MNI). However, the experimental paradigm investigates creative generation and evaluation during book-cover illustration design — an open-ended creative task — rather than an explicit problem-solving task as defined by the review (a goal-directed task requiring planning/sequence of operations within a rule set to arrive at a correct or specific solution). The manuscript does not frame the task as solving a defined problem with a correct/target solution or apply explicit task constraints characteristic of typical problem-solving paradigms. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. All other inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only references and metadata provided). Cannot verify core methods, participants, or results. Therefore cannot confirm any inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria not met/unknown: I5 (unclear whether task meets the review's definition of problem solving), I6 (no information on whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates not reported in the provided content), I8 (no confirmation of BOLD or rCBF analysis details), I9 (voxelwise results not accessible in the provided content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confirmed from the available text. Because the full article content is missing, exclude pending retrieval of complete full text.

Full text incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, this is a task-based PET study on deductive vs probabilistic reasoning, so it meets I5 (task-based problem-solving/logical reasoning) and I8 (reports rCBF results). However, the available content does not confirm I6 (at least one whole-brain analysis with group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space), or I9 (voxelwise/coordinate results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on provided information. Per screening rules, because not all inclusion criteria can be verified and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Paced Visual Serial Addition Task (PVSAT) which involves goal-directed arithmetic/working-memory operations and thus meets I5. The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain analyses in healthy control adults (I6) and uses BOLD fMRI sequences (I8). Voxelwise results are presented in figures/tables describing activated Brodmann areas (I9). However, the manuscript as provided does not report stereotactic coordinates (x,y,z) in Talairach or MNI space for the reported activations — only Brodmann areas, Z-scores and cluster sizes are given — therefore I7 is not satisfied. Because not all inclusion criteria are met (I7 missing), the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study using mental arithmetic (three-digit addition/subtraction), which qualifies as a problem-solving task involving goal-directed calculation, planning/sequencing and rule-based operations. It includes a healthy control group with group-level whole-brain analyses (one-sample t-tests in controls and ANCOVA), reports task-related BOLD results, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of methods and results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, not solely disease/age/gender comparisons, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This study is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults and reports BOLD activation, but the experimental task is spatial perspective-taking/mental rotation (left-right judgments about a figure) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). Thus inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met. Additionally, the provided full text does not clearly report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) in the excerpt, so I7 cannot be confirmed from the supplied content. The study does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults) and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded.

This fMRI study examines mental arithmetic problems that require goal-directed calculation and procedural operations (carrying/borrowing), meeting the review definition of problem solving. It used a whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis in healthy adult participants (n=16). Data were normalized to MNI305 stereotactic space and analyzed with voxelwise thresholds (SPM99), and BOLD fMRI was used, satisfying stereotactic coordinate reporting and BOLD criteria. Voxelwise results are reported in group analyses and supported by individual subject maps, consistent with allowance for coordinates in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, includes healthy-group task effects, and is not limited to ROIs or only between-group clinical comparisons. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results and discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=23) using series-completion inductive reasoning tasks that meet the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed rule identification and execution to arrive at a previously unknown solution). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, BOLD fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task-related activations. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the full text. The study is not limited to ROI-only results and includes voxelwise whole-brain contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata available). From the abstract, the study is a task-based PET investigation of mental calculation (meets I5) and reports regional cerebral blood flow measures (meets I8). However, I cannot confirm that the study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses in healthy adults (I6) or that it reports task-related stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space (I7). I also cannot confirm that qualifying voxelwise results are available in tables/figures/supplement (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on the provided content. Because multiple required inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, I exclude this study pending access to the complete article.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n=42) using mental arithmetic (multiplication and subtraction), which constitutes a goal-directed, rule-based problem-solving task. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and cluster/FWE thresholds, and describes BOLD acquisition and voxelwise results in tables/figures. ROI analyses are also present but do not replace the whole-brain results. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

Although the study is a task-based fMRI investigation of mathematical problem solving in healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain group analyses and BOLD results, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space (no coordinate tables or explicit coordinate listings are present in the supplied content). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI problem-solving), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results are described and shown in figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no explicit stereotactic coordinates in the provided text to confirm coordinate-based reporting). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete, so not marked incomplete. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I7 (reporting of stereotactic coordinates) based on the provided material.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates solving arithmetic problems (multiplication and division). The tasks meet the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed calculation, planning/sequence of operations within an algebraic framework). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM2, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for task-related activations, and uses BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are reported and ROI analyses are supplementary. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI (BOLD) study in healthy adults that examines goal-directed, context-dependent navigation requiring retrieval, evaluation, planning and sequencing of actions (disambiguation of overlapping routes), which fits the review's operational definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level, whole-brain analyses (random-effects SPMs), uses MNI normalization and provides stereotactic coordinates and cluster results for task contrasts and connectivity differences, and presents BOLD-based beta-series correlation connectivity results. All required reporting formats (whole-brain results, coordinates in standardized space, BOLD analysis) are present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not clinical or non-empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based BOLD fMRI study using a subtraction task that requires complex problem solving (borrowing/estimation), satisfying I5. It includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and presents group activation maps for healthy adult controls (age 20-26), satisfying I6. Results are reported in Talairach stereotactic space (I7) and include BOLD-related regression coefficients/percent signal change (I8). Voxelwise results are presented in figures/tables (I9). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only (whole-brain voxelwise maps are reported), healthy-group task effects are presented, and this is an empirical human neuroimaging study. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on whole-brain, task-based fMRI studies of problem-solving in healthy adults.

The study is a task-based BOLD fMRI experiment in healthy adults that explicitly implemented a goal-directed problem-solving simulation task (participants imagined solving problems and formulating plans), satisfying the review's problem-solving definition. It reports whole-brain, group-level (random-effects) GLM analyses and seed PLS functional connectivity, with stereotactic MNI coordinates provided for activations (e.g., PCC, DLPFC). Voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in the main text and supplementary materials. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This PET study reports a task-based investigation of semantic decision-making (and syllable decisions) that the authors frame and interpret as involving complex/‘verbal problem-solving’ and relational semantic reasoning. It meets imaging and reporting requirements: healthy adult sample (n=19), group-level whole-brain PET (rCBF) analyses using SPM99, stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space, and voxelwise results presented in figures/tables. The semantic task entails goal-directed selection among alternatives and controlled semantic elaboration (consistent with the review’s definition of problem solving, including semantic problem-solving). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, coordinates) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that uses an arithmetic (addition) manipulation task requiring participants to compute sums (a goal-directed operation using rule-based arithmetic procedures), satisfying the meta-analysis definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses of BOLD data, uses MNI stereotactic space for localization, and provides activation foci (coordinates) and statistical thresholds. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=13) that reports whole-brain, group-level analyses and BOLD results. The cognitive task includes serial subtraction (arithmetic) performed as part of a divided-attention paradigm; arithmetic/problem-solving operations fit the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed operations within an algebraic/arithmetic rule set). Images were transformed to Talairach space and group voxelwise activation (Table 2, Fig. 1) is reported, satisfying stereotactic coordinate reporting. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This is an event-related whole-brain BOLD fMRI study of deductive reasoning (logical problem solving) in healthy adult participants. The task requires evaluating the validity of arguments (a goal-directed logical problem-solving task using formal rule sets), with behavioral validation of complexity and response times. Group-level whole-brain mixed-effects analyses are reported, with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and tables of activation foci, and BOLD fMRI contrasts (complex>simple, reading, valid>invalid, etc.). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London planning/problem-solving task (meets problem-solving definition). It reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adult participants, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for activation foci, and uses BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are reported and visualized. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study using H2 15O measuring regional cerebral blood flow during the Tower of London planning task (a problem-solving paradigm). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM (normalization to stereotaxic space) and lists activation tables/figures (stereotactic coordinates referenced to standard space). Participants are healthy adults (n=6). rCBF analyses are reported and correlational/contrast results are presented. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based PET problem-solving studies and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of imagined egocentric transformations (hand and perspective rotation) in healthy adults. While it includes whole-brain, group-level analyses reported in MNI space and BOLD results, the tasks are mental rotation/spatial-visualization and handedness/left–right judgments rather than goal-directed problem-solving as defined in the review (i.e., requiring identification/planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution within a rule-based problem-solving framework). Therefore it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes mental serial subtraction (a problem-solving arithmetic task), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise BOLD results and shows activation maps/voxelwise results in figures. However, the paper does NOT report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations in the text, tables, or supplement, which is required by inclusion criterion I7. Therefore it cannot be included in the meta-analysis despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of reasoning/problem solving using Raven-like matrix problems in healthy adult participants. The study used whole-brain, group-level analyses (SPM99) on data from eight healthy adults, reports BOLD-related fMRI results, and provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) in tables and figures. Voxelwise results and contrasts (including linear-trend and subtractive contrasts) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not limited to ROIs, not a between-group-only or clinical comparison, and not a review). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria.

This study is an fMRI investigation of calendrical calculation and mental arithmetic and therefore meets I5 (task-based problem-solving-like tasks involving rule-based calculation), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). However, it does not meet I6: the paper does not report whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adult individuals — the imaging results are single-case/case-study (two autistic savants and a single normal participant) rather than a healthy adult group analysis. This violates the requirement for group-level healthy adult effects. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the study does not include a healthy-group task effect (no healthy adult group-level contrasts). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded.

Experiment 2 reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=25) using a compound remote-associate problem-solving task (clear goal and cognitive operations to reach a solution). The analysis used whole-brain, random-effects group-level BOLD contrasts comparing preparation for insight vs noninsight, with cluster-based voxelwise results and a table of clusters (Table 1) indicating stereotactic results. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based problem solving), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinate results reported in cluster table), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (coordinates presented in table). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only between-group comparisons, empirical human data). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore INCLUDE.

Empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using the Tower of London planning/problem-solving task (goal-directed planning). Whole-brain, random-effects group analyses are reported (ANOVA, random-effects), with voxelwise stereotactic coordinates given in MNI (and converted to Talairach) and task-related BOLD results. Voxelwise results are reported and thresholds described. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This task (PASAT) requires goal-directed arithmetic operations—maintaining and manipulating sequential numbers and applying addition rules under time constraints—meeting the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults (N=15) with group-level (second-level) whole-brain analyses (I6). fMRI BOLD methods and analyses are reported throughout (I8). The paper describes normalization to MNI space and SPM localization procedures and reports activations localized to specific brain regions (lobule VII, prefrontal areas), consistent with reporting stereotactic results in standardized space (I7); voxelwise results are described in figures/tables as implied by the methods/results (I9). The full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that required goal-directed planning, sequencing, and execution to reach a hidden goal (encoding a map, planning a route, using self-motion cues to navigate). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t tests and contrasts), uses BOLD fMRI, normalizes data to MNI space (coordinates/tables provided), and presents voxelwise results in tables and figures. The task meets the review definition of problem solving (goal plus need to compute and execute actions to reach it). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level analyses that report stereotactic coordinates (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied). However, the task used (mental rotation) is a visuospatial transformation task rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing operations within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical frameworks). Therefore I5 is not met and the study does not address the review's problem-solving objective. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of algebraic problem solving in healthy adults (N=18) that directly examines problem-solving strategies (symbolic vs. model) and the neural correlates of representing and validating solutions. It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses, BOLD fMRI data acquired on a 3T scanner, and states data were transformed into Talairach space with reported ROI maxima and activation clusters (results referenced in tables/figures). The study therefore meets the review’s requirements for a problem-solving task (I5), whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic reporting in Talairach space (I7), BOLD analysis (I8), and acceptable reporting of voxelwise results in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is an animal pharmacokinetic PET study of a radiolabeled drug (GTS-21) in baboons and mice, not a task-based neuroimaging investigation of problem solving in healthy adult humans. It contains no task paradigm meeting the review's problem-solving definition, no healthy adult human group-level whole-brain analysis, no stereotactic activation coordinates, and no task-related BOLD or task-based rCBF contrasts. Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). Although it is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results in MNI space (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task is a forced-choice preference selection between abstract value words reflecting moral/value orientation, not a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm as defined in I5. Participants made spontaneous preference judgments rather than engaging in identifying/planning/sequencing actions or applying rule-based operations to reach a correct or novel solution. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED because I5 is not satisfied; other inclusion criteria (I6,I7,I8,I9) are met.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of mathematical problem solving in healthy adults (and adolescents), using whole-brain analyses and reporting BOLD-based results. It therefore satisfies I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain/group-level effects in healthy adults), and I8 (BOLD analysis). The manuscript includes whole-brain activation maps/figures, so I9 (accepting voxelwise results in figures/supplement) appears satisfied. However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) or explicitly state coordinate tables/supplementary coordinate lists; I7 is not met in the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is not satisfied in the available full text, the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that operationalises problem solving as probabilistic/inductive reasoning (constructing competing hypotheses and selecting the best fit), which fits the review's problem-solving definition. The paper reports a group-level whole-brain (fixed-effects) voxelwise analysis, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI→Talairach) of activation peaks, and reports BOLD (fMRI) results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Although the sample is small and analyses are fixed-effects (not random-effects), the study nonetheless meets the stated inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses a task in which subjects must mentally navigate from one place to another, requiring a goal and planning/sequencing of turns (meets problem-solving definition). It is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants (16 right-handed males) with group-level whole-brain random-effects analysis. The paper reports activation peaks (voxelwise results) across subjects, which implies stereotactic coordinate reporting (results/peaks/tables/figures available), and BOLD signal analysis was used. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group/disease comparison only, and not non-empirical). Although explicit coordinate numbers are not shown in the provided excerpt, the text states detected peaks and group-level random-effects results, consistent with inclusion criterion I7/I9. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

The fMRI study reports a goal-directed task (count visible balls from either own or avatar perspective) that requires mental spatial transformation and execution of operations to arrive at a correct response, satisfying the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The study includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI analyses (I8). Task-related voxelwise results are presented in text/tables and ROI/whole-brain contrasts (I9). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper presents whole-brain results (not ROI-only), reports healthy-group task effects, and is an original empirical fMRI study. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task-based neuroimaging studies of problem-solving across domains.

This manuscript is a narrative synthesis summarizing multiple PET and fMRI studies conducted by the authors’ laboratory (not a primary empirical report presenting novel whole-brain coordinate tables). Although it describes task-based mental-arithmetic stress paradigms (MIST) used in PET and fMRI with group-level BOLD/rCBF findings in healthy adults, the paper itself functions as a review and does not present new stereotactic coordinate tables or primary whole-brain coordinate results required for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical/review without original coordinate data). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (describes task-based problem-solving/mental-arithmetic tasks) and I8 (reports BOLD and rCBF analyses in the described studies). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no stereotactic Talairach/MNI coordinates reported in this article), I9 (no explicit coordinates in tables/figures/supplementary materials indicated). I6 is partially addressed (group-level effects are described) but as the article is a review, primary whole-brain coordinate results are not provided. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16) that examines deductive/transitive reasoning (logical validity judgments), which qualifies as a problem-solving task (goal-directed evaluation using rule-based logic). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM2) and discusses stereotactic results (MNI coordinates/Z-values) with imaging results reported in the manuscript (tables/figures referenced). All required inclusion criteria are met (I5: problem-solving logical task; I6: whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults; I7: stereotactic coordinate results in MNI space; I8: BOLD fMRI analysis; I9: coordinates/results available in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are triggered: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to disease/age/gender contrasts, and include within-group healthy task effects. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore include.

This study uses a task-based fMRI Tower of London planning paradigm that fulfills the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a solution). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses for adult participants (including separate main-effect maps for OCS low scoring twins, i.e., healthy adults). Results are reported as voxelwise BOLD effects with MNI stereotactic coordinates presented in tables and figures. Voxelwise whole-brain analyses (including task vs baseline and task-load contrasts) are explicitly described and thresholding/cluster criteria provided. Although the sample comprises twins discordant for obsessive–compulsive symptoms (with a few meeting OCD criteria), the paper provides healthy-group task effects and whole-brain coordinate results, meeting inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract provided). From the abstract, the study is a task-based PET study of deductive reasoning/training so I5 is met. However, I cannot verify critical inclusion criteria: I6 (presence of at least one whole-brain, group-level analysis in healthy adults) is not clearly reported in the abstract; I7 (stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach/MNI) is not stated; I8 (reports BOLD or rCBF analysis details/results) is not confirmed. No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract. Because the full article (methods, results, coordinate tables) is not provided, I cannot confirm the remaining required criteria, so the study is excluded pending full text. Inclusion IDs met: I5. Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I6, I7, I8. Exclusion IDs met: none ([]).

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD stereotactic coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task is associative memory/label identification (learned mapping of four chords to numerals) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed generation/planning/sequencing of novel solutions or critical evaluation operations). The task involves retrieval of learned conditional associations and motor responses, not formulation or execution of strategies to solve a presented problem. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study does not satisfy the required problem-solving task criterion (I5) and must be excluded.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI effects in healthy adults) and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 — tasks reported (verbal learning, simple arithmetic, divided attention) are not operationalized as 'problem-solving' tasks per the review definition (goal-directed planning/sequencing/evaluation to arrive at a novel or rule-based solution); I7 — the article text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI); I9 — no voxelwise coordinate results (tables/figures/supplement) are provided in the full text supplied. Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria (notably I5, I7, I9) and must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based O-15 PET study that used a goal-directed navigation task (find a predefined destination in a VR maze), which meets the provided operational definition of problem solving (goal, planning/sequencing actions, execution to reach an outcome). It includes healthy adult participants with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) reporting stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space and regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) results. Voxelwise results are presented and thresholded, with coordinates and figures described. All required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: the study is not ROI-only, includes within-group healthy task effects (not only between-group contrasts), and is original empirical work. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly investigates logical problem solving (generation of deductive conclusions), which fits the review’s definition of problem solving. It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (conjunction and contrasts) with normalization to MNI space and cluster-corrected results, and uses BOLD fMRI. Coordinate results and supplementary data are indicated. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a between-group clinical comparison, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only title, abstract, and metadata provided). From the abstract: the study used task-based fMRI arithmetic tasks that meet I5 (arithmetic computation qualifies as a problem-solving task) and I6 (group-level whole-brain activation effects are described). The use of fMRI satisfies I8 (BOLD analysis) as reported. However, I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space) cannot be verified because coordinate tables/locations are not present in the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are evident from the abstract. Because reporting stereotactic coordinates (I7) is required and cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a mental-arithmetic task that requires goal-directed operations (repeated subtraction) and thus meets the review's definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM99, presents BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (e.g., x=−34,y=−42,z=42) with tables/figures, and includes BOLD analyses and functional connectivity. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-only, non-empirical) apply.

This is a PET receptor-occupancy study using [11C]-raclopride measuring D2 occupancy and cognitive performance in healthy volunteers. It does not perform task-based whole-brain analyses of problem-solving; imaging analyses are ROI-based (striatal, cerebellar, substantia nigra) for binding potential and occupancy, not task-evoked BOLD/rCBF contrasts reported as stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it fails the review inclusions. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI results). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based problem-solving paradigm as defined), I6 (no whole-brain group-level imaging analysis), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results for task activations), I8 (no BOLD or rCBF task analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task (a problem-solving paradigm). It reports whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses (planning minus subtracting contrast) in healthy older adults, with BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for significant clusters (e.g., left SPC [−36 −56 52]) and FWE-corrected statistics. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full. No ROI-only reporting or exclusionary features are present. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for a whole-brain, task-based fMRI study of problem-solving in healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study of clinical reasoning (answering vignette-based MCQs), which constitutes a problem-solving task (goal: determine diagnosis; requires evaluation, planning/selection and execution to arrive at a correct answer). The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with group-level effects (experts vs novices), uses BOLD fMRI (EPI), and reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (figures/tables). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study of logical problem solving (identifying contradictions using Aristotelian premise-conclusion pairs) in healthy adult participants. The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects fMRI analyses (SPM8), BOLD results, and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for task-related increases. Voxelwise results are reported in the main text/figures and small-volume corrections are applied. The experimental task fits the problem-solving definition (goal-directed logical evaluation and application of rule set). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

While this is an event-related task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that reports BOLD results with whole-brain analyses and stereotactic normalization, the experimental task is a two-card gambling paradigm examining counterfactual thinking, reward and emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis is reported), I7 (data normalized to Talairach space and coordinates are provided for ROIs/clusters), and I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the task is a gambling/decision-making paradigm and does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (no evidence of a goal requiring planning/sequencing or critical thinking processes to identify/execute a solution algorithmically or to arrive at a novel/correct solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I5.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using forced-choice reasoning tasks (temperature and poverty) that require goal-directed reasoning/ problem-solving processes to arrive at correct answers. The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses using SPM2, provides stereotactic coordinates (ICBM/MNI space), and measures BOLD signal (fMRI). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided, and voxelwise results are reported in tables/figures. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of conditional reasoning (Wason selection-style rule-broken task) in 24 healthy adults, employing whole-brain analyses (SPM2 random-effects, FWE/FDR corrections) and reporting region-level activations normalized to MNI space. The task requires applying logical/rule-based operations to determine rule violations, fitting the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed, rule-based evaluation/planning to reach correct judgments). BOLD fMRI analyses are reported. The main text references voxelwise activation results (BA labels and cluster-level statistics) and indicates normalization to MNI and use of standard stereotactic reporting, consistent with availability of coordinates in tables/figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-healthy groups only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study uses a first-person virtual maze where subjects have a goal and must determine routes/decisions to reach it, meeting the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (planning/sequencing/navigation). It includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses for healthy control participants, reports task-related BOLD results with stereotactic Talairach coordinates (e.g., 18 -61 40), and presents voxelwise whole-brain maps and VOI analyses. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation of categorical vs. coordinate spatial encoding during active navigation in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is spatial memory/navigation encoding, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review—there is no focus on identifying/performing critical thinking processes to evaluate a problem, plan/sequencing actions to derive a solution within semantic/algebraic/logical frameworks), and I7 (the provided full text does not clearly report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space in the text supplied). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet the key problem-solving task requirement (I5) and does not clearly report stereotactic coordinates in the supplied content (I7).

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports results using anatomically- and functionally-defined ROI analyses rather than a whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of a problem-solving task — mental calculation/arithmetic fits the defined problem-solving framework) and I8 (reports BOLD/fMRI analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no evidence of a whole-brain group-level analysis reported), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates in the provided text or tables/figures), I9 (no indication that voxelwise coordinate results are available elsewhere). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given that E3 excludes studies that report only ROI results, this study must be excluded.

This study does not meet the review's problem-solving task requirement (I5). The fMRI tasks are Theory of Mind (self-perspective inhibition) and a stop-signal response-inhibition task, which do not meet the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel or rule-based solution). The full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults reported), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm as defined). No exclusion criteria were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to failure to satisfy I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study of numerical inductive reasoning using a number-series completion task that requires identifying underlying rules and generating solutions — matching the review definition of problem solving. Participants were healthy adult volunteers. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise fMRI analyses (flexible factorial ANOVA and group t-tests) with results in stereotactic space (MNI coordinates) and BOLD contrasts, and also provides ROI analyses; voxelwise results are thresholded and reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a between-group-disease comparison, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults and includes an explicit mental-calculation localizer (silent subtraction) that constitutes a problem-solving task (applying arithmetic rules to reach a solution). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed and reported, with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD contrasts (calculation > sentence comprehension). Healthy adult participants (n=14) were used. Thus it meets I5 (problem-solving task: mental calculation), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates are reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adults using a mental arithmetic task that meets the definition of problem-solving (goal-directed arithmetic operations within a rule set). It reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) with group-level effects in healthy adults, provides stereotactic coordinates for rCBF increases, and reports regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) PET results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is complete. The study uses task-based fMRI with whole-brain analyses in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results; however, the experimental paradigm is a working memory (listening/reading span and word-recognition) task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed evaluation/planning/sequencing to reach a solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD analysis), I9 (qualifying voxelwise results are available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is working memory, not problem-solving). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Given that ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I5 is not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This is a patient fMRI case study of number processing after left ventral occipito-temporal damage. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (study includes whole-brain second-level analyses with a healthy control group), I7 (reports MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Primary inclusion criterion not met: I5. The tasks are semantic/magnitude comparisons (quantity: larger/smaller; category: summer/winter; and a color-perceptual task) and do not constitute the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed multi-step planning, sequencing, critical evaluation or execution toward a novel solution). The paper’s focus is on compensatory neural mechanisms in a stroke patient rather than investigating problem-solving across domains in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=22 for fMRI) using problem-solving tasks (Cattell Culture Fair and Letter Sets ‘odd-one-out’ high-g items) that require goal-directed reasoning, rule application, and novel problem solving, meeting the review definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses of BOLD fMRI data with activations for high-g versus low-g contrasts (whole-brain FDR thresholding) and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (normalization to MNI/ICBM template; peak coordinates reported). BOLD contrast and voxelwise results are presented and ROI/whole-ROI analyses supplement the voxelwise findings. Thus all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (results are not ROI-only, not limited to clinical/age/gender group comparisons, not only between-group contrasts, and this is an original empirical report). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=13) using a goal-directed maze navigation task that requires planning, sequential decision-making, and execution to reach a goal (qualifies as problem-solving). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (random-effects) were performed, BOLD fMRI was used, and stereotactic coordinates are reported (e.g., MNI x,y,z = -32,49,-1). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not group-comparison-only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of deductive problem solving (syllogisms) in healthy adults. It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses using SPM8 with normalization to MNI space and voxelwise BOLD contrasts (integration effect), provides stereotactic coordinates (e.g. −42 14 20), and reports significant task-related activations (voxel-level FWE-corrected). Thus it satisfies I5–I9. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This study does not investigate problem-solving as defined by the review. It reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain group analyses (I6) and BOLD measures (I8). However, the tasks used are a false-belief (Theory of Mind) paradigm and a Go/No-go inhibitory control task, which do not meet the review's problem-solving definition (I5 not met). The provided full text does not include stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI coordinates in the excerpt (I7 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply based on the provided content. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I5 (and I7 is not clearly satisfied in the provided text).

Excluded because the task studied is moral decision-making/ToM/empathy, not a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5 not met). The study does meet other methodological inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults (I6), BOLD fMRI (I8), and the manuscript indicates voxelwise results/tables/supplementary are available (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the provided full text. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an fMRI investigation of theory-of-mind/intentionality (mental state reasoning) using sentence-reading tasks; it does not investigate problem-solving as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations, or execution of operations to reach a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in standardized stereotactic space/Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task-based study of problem solving). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only report, no clinical-group-only contrasts, not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED because it does not address problem-solving tasks per I5.

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adult participants that used a logical reasoning task meeting the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed logical reasoning with rule-based responses). Whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses were performed at the group level (INHIB and LOGIC groups). The study reports regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) task-related analyses and refers to peak (stereotactic) coordinates and conjunction maps (voxelwise results presented in maps/figures), satisfying requirements for reporting standardized coordinates/voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, clinical-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core data appear present.

Full text/PDF is not accessible in the provided content. The abstract shows a task-based fMRI 'mental maze' (consistent with problem solving; I5) and fMRI implies BOLD analysis (I8). However, critical details required by the review cannot be verified: the manuscript as provided does not allow confirmation of a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis in healthy adults (I6), nor whether stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task-related increases are reported (I7) or whether voxelwise results/tables/figures are available (I9). No explicit exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract. Because I6 and I7 (and I9) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be included at this stage.

This study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). It reports a spatial judgement/mental imagery task (Mental Clock Test) requiring angle discrimination, which is a perceptual/attentional judgement rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing or execution of operations to derive a previously unknown solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI random-effects analysis in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results and coordinates reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Therefore excluded because I5 not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes the Tower of London (planning/problem-solving) task, which meets the definition of problem-solving (goal-directed planning and sequencing to reach a solution). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and reports BOLD fMRI results (with coordinates in main text and supplementary material). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of numeric comparison (positive, negative, mixed number pairs) in healthy adults with whole-brain BOLD analyses, but the task is a speeded magnitude comparison rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the task does not require goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing or generating previously unknown solutions; it is a comparison/decision task applying learned numeric rules). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded on the basis that I5 is not satisfied.

This task-based fMRI study includes the Tower of London planning task, which meets the definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning and sequencing). It reports BOLD-based fMRI analyses, performs whole-brain SPM group-level analyses normalized to MNI space (with whole-brain FDR correction and rendered statistical parametric maps), and includes healthy adult control participants with group-level task effects and patient-control comparisons. Voxelwise/whole-brain results are presented as statistical maps (figures) and ROI and region-level coordinates are provided (e.g., MNI coordinates for ROIs), satisfying the requirement that stereotactic/MNI-referenced task-related activations are reported or available. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition / Theory of Mind using a naturalistic video-based MASC paradigm, not a problem‑solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule‑based operations to find a solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem solving task) is NOT met. The study does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete (only retraction notice and metadata available). Cannot verify that the study meets required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (cannot confirm a task-based problem-solving paradigm from available text), I6 (cannot confirm whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (cannot confirm stereotactic coordinate reporting), I8 (cannot confirm BOLD or rCBF analysis), I9 (cannot confirm availability of voxelwise coordinate results). Exclusion criteria met: none identifiable from provided material. Because the full article content (methods, results) is unavailable, all inclusion criteria cannot be evaluated and the record must be excluded. fulltext_incomplete takes precedence.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using a modified beads probabilistic reasoning task that requires goal-directed evidence gathering and decision-making (evaluating information, planning when to stop, and executing responses), fitting the operational definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and voxelwise contrasts (task blocks vs control; last vs preceding stimuli), provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for activations, and includes ROI analyses but not exclusively. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9, and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). The fMRI task is a theory-of-mind (mental state reasoning) Person-Description/False-Belief paradigm (thoughts/emotions vs appearance), which does not involve goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations, or rule-based solution generation required by the meta-analysis definition of problem solving. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain analyses with group-level effects in healthy adult individuals are reported), I7 (results reported in MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported), I9 (voxelwise/whole-brain results presented in main text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria applied: none (no E3–E6 violations). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a single-subject (one 16-year-old) EEG/fMRI case study of mental addition. While the study uses task-based whole-brain fMRI with BOLD analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates (satisfying I5, I7, I8, I9), it does NOT include any group-level effects in healthy adults (no group of healthy adult participants). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (doesn't include any healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Exclusion IDs met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no group-level healthy adult data).

The study used the Paced Visual Serial Addition Test (PVSAT), a working memory/processing-speed task, rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel solution). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. It does meet I6 (includes healthy adult group-level whole-brain analyses), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/supplementary). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract provided). Abstract shows this is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults including a verbal-reasoning (analogies) task and a spatial task, and reports image-based (distributed/whole-brain) and ROI analyses. Inclusion criteria met from available information: I5 (contains a problem-solving verbal-analogies task), I6 (reports group-level whole-brain image-based analyses in healthy adults), and I8 (BOLD fMRI data). However I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI) and I9 (confirmation that voxelwise coordinate results are reported in text/tables/figures) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because the provided full text is incomplete and key criterion I7/I9 cannot be verified, I exclude this study pending full-text verification.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults examining relational reasoning/transitive inference, which constitutes a logical problem-solving task (deriving comparative relations and planning/sequence operations to infer novel relations). The study performed whole-brain, group-level mixed-effects analyses (FLAME), reports stereotactic peak coordinates in MNI space, and reports BOLD results. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical human data).

Full text is not available (fulltext_incomplete=true). Title indicates the study concerns relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), suggesting patient-focused work rather than task-based fMRI/PET in healthy adults. Based on available information: no inclusion criteria are demonstrably met. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or unverified: I5 (problem-solving task) - not verifiable; I6 (healthy adult group whole-brain effects) - likely not met given RRMS focus; I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported) - unknown; I8 (BOLD or rCBF analysis reported) - unknown; I9 (voxelwise results availability) - unknown. No exclusion criteria from the list can be confidently applied from the provided metadata. Because the full text is missing, I cannot verify methods/results; therefore the study is excluded from the review.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study of three-term relational reasoning (a logical problem-solving task requiring subjects to determine whether conclusions follow from premises), conducted in 14 healthy adult subjects with group-level, random-effects whole-brain analyses using SPM. The methods explicitly describe whole-brain preprocessing and voxelwise inference after normalization to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template, and the results section references voxelwise activations summarized in tables/figures (stereotactic results are indicated as available). The study reports BOLD (T2*-weighted) analyses and task-related activation increases. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a review, includes healthy-group task effects). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of mathematical problem solving (mental arithmetic) in healthy adults that fits the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed arithmetic operations following rule sets). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in a sample of healthy adults (N=18). Results include voxelwise BOLD activation and deactivation maps with stereotactic (MNI) peak coordinates presented in tables and figures. Voxelwise/whole-brain contrasts are reported (Calculation vs Identification; between-condition contrasts), and both activation and behavioral correlations are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not solely between-group/disease comparisons, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is task-based fMRI in healthy adults and tests goal-direction/navigation judgments which involve planning/simulation (meets I5). It reports whole-brain MVPA/searchlight group analyses (meets I6) and uses BOLD fMRI (meets I8). The manuscript indicates voxelwise results available in figures/supplement (meets I9). However, the provided full text does not report task-related stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach or MNI space (I7 not demonstrated in the content supplied). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, patient-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Because I7 is required and cannot be verified from the provided text, the study must be excluded. Full text appears otherwise complete in results/discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study is excluded because it does not study a problem-solving task (I5 not met). The fMRI task is an emotion/mood induction using IAPS, not goal-directed problem solving or critical-thinking/planning operations. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses including healthy adult controls), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of a problem-solving task (matchstick problems) reporting whole-brain voxelwise BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates, it does not provide whole-brain group-level task effects reported for healthy adults alone. Analyses are either across a mixed sample (adolescents + adults) or compare adolescents versus adults; the adults>adolescents contrast yielded no significant whole-brain activations. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I6 (no whole-brain group-level adult-only task effects reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI problem solving), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no adult-only whole-brain group-level task effect provided). Exclusion criteria met: none (the paper reports whole-brain analyses, not ROI-only). Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment of problem solving in healthy adults and includes whole-brain analyses and BOLD measures (meets I5, I6, I8). However, the provided full text does not report task-related stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for activation foci or voxelwise results in coordinate space, and I7 is thus not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Exclusion is based on failure to meet inclusion criterion I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting).

Although this is a whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD analyses, the task investigated (mental rotation and perspective taking) is a perceptual/spatial transformation task rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing or critical-thinking operations to reach a solution). The study does not involve identifying or performing critical thinking processes, planning/sequencing actions, or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a (novel) solution in the sense required by inclusion criterion I5. Therefore I5 is not met. All other inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study uses a serial addition (mental-operation numeral) task that meets the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed manipulation using arithmetic rules). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults (n=16) using SPM99 with normalization to the MNI template and voxelwise t-maps, and uses BOLD fMRI. The manuscript describes task-related activations and contrasts (MO-numeral vs VR and vs fixation); voxelwise results are indicated as available in standardized space (normalized to MNI) and are likely presented in figures/tables. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of anagram problem solving in healthy adult participants (N=15). The task meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed letter rearrangement requiring generation, evaluation, and planning of solutions). Whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses were performed (SPM2; normalization to MNI template) with voxelwise stereotactic coordinates reported for task-related BOLD activations. BOLD signal (fMRI) results are reported and coordinates are given in standard space. No exclusion criteria are violated. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an arithmetic problem-solving task (meets I5). It includes healthy adult participants (19–22 years) and reports group-level analyses comparing adults and children; task-related activation and ICA maps indicate whole-brain analyses were performed (meets I6). The paper clearly uses BOLD-fMRI (meets I8). The manuscript refers to ICA peak voxels and supplemental materials/figures for region locations and analytic results, indicating stereotactic peak/voxelwise results are available in figures/supplementary (meets I7 and acceptable reporting per I9). The study is empirical and not ROI-only (no exclusion criteria met). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary materials are referenced but absence does not render the main text incomplete.

This is a methods/VR-stimulus development paper reporting a spatial navigation/memory task (explore/memorize a virtual city) in 4 healthy adults with BOLD fMRI and group-level (fixed-effect) whole-brain analyses. It does not investigate or operationalize a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met — the paradigm is navigation/memory, not goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution). The paper does report BOLD analyses and group-level whole-brain results (I6 and I8 met), but stereotactic coordinate tables are not clearly provided in the supplied text (I7 not clearly met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I5 (and lacking clear evidence for I7).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: it does not provide a whole-brain, group-level analysis reported specifically for healthy adult participants only. The sample is mixed (adolescents and adults) and the primary whole-brain Relational>Control results reported in this full text are averaged across age groups (or used for developmental contrasts); adult-only stereotactic whole-brain results are not presented in the full text. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI relational reasoning fits the problem-solving definition), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates/MNI in tables), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results available in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no whole-brain group-level effects reported for healthy adults alone). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=18) that includes an arithmetic task using Reverse Polish notation which requires goal-directed, rule-based calculation (execution of operations to arrive at a correct result), meeting the review definition of problem solving. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (second-level SPM analyses, conjunctions), uses stereotactic normalization (MNI space) and reports voxelwise activation results and clusters (tables/figures). BOLD signal (fMRI) analyses are the main outcome. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, patient-only, non-empirical) are met. Inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied.

The study is an fMRI task of decision-making under uncertainty in an aviation-simulation landing task. It meets I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adult participants), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported), and I9 (voxelwise results and tables reported). However, it does not meet I5: the task is a binary decision/risk-taking task (landing vs. go-around) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (involving goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to reach a previously unknown solution). Therefore the study does not address the review’s problem-solving construct and must be excluded.

This is an empirical PET study of healthy adult participants (n=12) using a modified Tower of London task that requires goal-setting, planning, sequencing moves, and execution — meeting the review’s definition of problem-solving (I5). Analyses were performed at the group level across the whole brain (PET images normalized to a stereotaxic coordinate system), reporting stereotactic peak coordinates (x,y,z) and voxelwise rCBF results, satisfying I6, I7, and I8. Coordinate results and statistical maps are presented in the text/tables, consistent with I9. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs (E3), are not only between-group/disease comparisons (E4/E5), and the paper is original empirical research (not a review) (E6). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This is a behavioral study of arithmetic strategy ratings and reaction times; no fMRI or PET data were collected or reported. Therefore it does not meet the neuroimaging inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study of problem solving), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results reported), I8 (no BOLD or rCBF analyses reported), I9 (no voxelwise neuroimaging results provided). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the paper does not include any healthy-group task-related neuroimaging effects/contrasts). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion, but lacks any neuroimaging data. Hence excluded from the meta-analysis focused on whole-brain task-based fMRI/PET studies.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults reporting stereotactic coordinates, the experimental task is a two-digit number magnitude comparison (decide which of two numbers is larger). This is a perceptual/cognitive magnitude-comparison task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (which requires goal-directed planning, sequencing, evaluation, or execution of operations to arrive at a solution beyond a single-step comparison). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met. Inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8 are met (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults; stereotactic coordinates reported; BOLD fMRI analysis). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of spatial memory/navigation (pointing to a start location after traversing virtual mazes). It does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5): the authors explicitly state “As only one direction was possible at each turn, no route planning was required,” indicating no requirement for planning/sequencing or other critical problem-solving operations. The study does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported, e.g., XYZ = -34 -34 -6), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results available in supplementary material). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Thus the paper must be excluded because it fails I5 (problem-solving task).

This manuscript reports task-based fMRI experiments using Compound Remote Associate (CRA) problem-solving in healthy adults (meets I5), includes group-level whole-brain event-related fMRI analyses (meets I6), and reports task-related BOLD effects (meets I8).
