However, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate results (Talairach or MNI) or explicit voxelwise coordinate tables/figures in the content supplied, so I7 (reporting coordinates) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on the provided text. Because failure to report standardized stereotactic coordinates is a required inclusion criterion, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete for methods and narrative results, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of deductive reasoning (logical and linguistic inference) in healthy adult participants. The inference tasks involve evaluating validity (goal-directed logical problem solving), fitting the review's definition of problem solving using logical rules. The study reports group-level whole-brain mixed-effects analyses with BOLD contrast maps, stereotactic (MNI) normalization, and voxelwise results (tables and SI). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task: logical deduction), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in standardized space), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/SI). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of non-conscious visual working memory and delayed orientation discrimination; it does not investigate problem-solving as defined in I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing or performing critical thinking to generate novel solutions across semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule sets). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. It does satisfy other methodological criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and includes BOLD analyses (I8); voxelwise results are reported (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of a problem-solving task (Chinese chess checkmate problems). The task has a clear goal (find a checkmate), requires planning/sequencing moves and rule-based operations, matching the review’s problem-solving definition. Participants are healthy adult groups (grandmasters/masters and novices). The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses with random-effects group-level one-sample and two-sample t-tests, uses BOLD fMRI (task-based contrasts), and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and voxelwise (AlphaSim-corrected) maps. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to disease/age/gender group comparisons, include within-group healthy task effects, and it is empirical primary research. The full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This J. Neurosci. article reports task-based fMRI of fluid reasoning (Raven's matrices/reasoning tasks) in healthy young adults, constituting a problem-solving task. The study performed whole-brain, group-level analyses using SPM2 and reported BOLD activation maps associated with reasoning; it references statistical maps and supplemental tables/figures (available at the journal website), satisfying the requirement that stereotactic coordinate results are available in the paper/supplement. The sample comprises healthy adults and the analyses report task-related increases and predictive group-level effects. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical-group comparisons only, empirical original data). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=17) using a transitive logical-reasoning task (indeterminate/determinate trials). The task involves applying logical rules to determine validity of conclusions, fitting the review definition of problem solving (I5). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., 42,20,-8) and BOLD/fMRI results (I6–I8). Results and coordinates are reported in the main text and tables (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group patient comparison only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes explicit route-planning tasks (customer-driven route planning) that meet the review's definition of problem solving: subjects are given a goal and must plan/sequence actions to reach it. The study used whole-brain, group-level analyses (random-effects SPM2), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and presents BOLD-based results (EPI BOLD contrast) with tables of activations. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-group-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

This article is a commentary/review summarizing Eger et al.’s fMRI findings rather than reporting original empirical human neuroimaging data. Exclusion ID met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original human data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study of a defined problem-solving task), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults reported), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (no BOLD or rCBF analyses presented), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate results available). The full text provided contains introduction/discussion-style content and lacks methods, participants, results, tables of coordinates, or neuroimaging analyses necessary to satisfy inclusion criteria. fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a mental calculation (multiplication) task that constitutes an algebraic/problem-solving task. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (task vs rest), provides BOLD fMRI results, and lists peak activation coordinates in MNI space (e.g., left intraparietal sulcus x = −34, y = −50, z = 48). Voxelwise results and supplementary data are indicated. Sample consists of healthy adult participants. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes a Tower of London (ToL) planning paradigm which fits the review’s definition of problem solving (explicit goal, planning/sequencing moves, executing operations under rules to arrive at a solution). Whole-brain, group-level analyses are reported (main effects and group comparisons), healthy adult controls are included, and BOLD fMRI contrasts and voxelwise results are reported in figures/tables (e.g., Table 3 and SPM results described). Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

The study is an fMRI investigation of decision-making/risk estimation (a gambling 'cake' task) in children and adults. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (includes whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adult participants), I7 (reports stereotactic results / MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results available in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the task is a gambling/decision-making task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review—there is no evidence the task required goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing or executing operations within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule-sets to derive a previously unknown solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded for failure to meet I5.

The study does not meet the review’s operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task involved rating the ‘reasonableness’ of partisan statements (judgment/evaluation), not engaging goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution. It does meet inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses). However, the provided full text does not explicitly report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space (I7) within the supplied content, so I7 is not confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the provided text. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet I5 (and I7 is not verifiable from the provided content).

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task, which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning and sequencing of moves). The study includes healthy adult control subjects and reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (main effects in controls and group interactions). Results are reported as BOLD signal changes and presented with stereotactic coordinates (Talairach space) in tables/figures. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of passive conceptual expansion/metaphor processing (creative cognition) and does not employ a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined by I5 (no requirement to identify/plan/execute steps to reach a goal or arrive at a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (healthy adult group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses), I7 (results reported in stereotactic space / standard reporting conventions), I8 (BOLD fMRI reported), I9 (voxelwise results acceptable). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is semantic/metaphor judgment, not a problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing to reach a goal). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore exclude for not meeting I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain group analyses and BOLD results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in standardized space, MNI), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), I9 (voxelwise results/whole-brain contrasts reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review — tasks are economic game, moral/intentional judgment, and Theory of Mind/story judgments rather than goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing to reach a solution). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although this task-based fMRI study examines problem-solving tasks (calendrical calculation and division) in a healthy adult and reports MNI-normalized BOLD results and connectivity/voxelwise analyses, it is a single-subject (n=1) study and does not provide group-level whole-brain effects. Inclusion criterion I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adult individuals) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants that reports whole-brain group-level BOLD results in standardized (MNI) space (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task probes moral judgment/decision-making (assessing emotional aversiveness, utilitarian outcomes, and overall moral acceptability) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., having a goal that requires figuring out a way to reach it via planning/sequencing or operations to arrive at a novel or correct solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study of heuristic problem solving (simplified Sudoku) in healthy adults (n=15 analyzed). It uses whole-brain voxelwise ANOVA across conditions (group-level effects) and reports BOLD analyses. The data were coregistered to the Talairach coordinate system and the manuscript indicates ROI locations/sizes in the Appendix, satisfying stereotactic reporting. Voxelwise results are presented via figures/tables and multivariate classification results are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of causal inference during narrative reading (inference generation/integration), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). Although it uses task-based BOLD fMRI (I8 met) in healthy adults, the analysis is ROI-based with anatomically defined ROIs and limited slice coverage rather than a whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis (E3 and I6 not met). The paper does not report stereotactic coordinates for task-related activations in standardized space (I7 not met). Therefore it does not meet all inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From available content: I8 is satisfied (task-based fMRI → BOLD analysis). However I5 is not clearly met—sentence–picture verification is a verification/comprehension task and the abstract does not establish that it is a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a solution). I6 cannot be confirmed: the abstract does not explicitly state a whole-brain group-level analysis. I7 cannot be confirmed: stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) are not reported in the abstract. No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly met based on the provided content. Because required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7) are not confirmed and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending full-text review.

This is an exclusion because the task is an antisaccade/error-processing paradigm (inhibitory oculomotor control and error-related dACC activation), not a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing, and executing operations to arrive at a correct/novel solution). Additionally, the full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space (I7 not satisfied). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain analyses with group-level effects including healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results presented in figures/whole-brain maps). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review. It uses a color-word Stroop inhibitory control task to probe error processing and insight in cocaine use disorder, not tasks requiring goal-directed problem identification, planning/sequencing, and solution generation across domains. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (performs whole-brain group-level analyses including healthy control participants), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does NOT study a problem-solving task per the review definition). Exclusion criteria met: none (does not meet E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on problem-solving in healthy adults.

Excluded because the study does not investigate problem-solving as defined in I5. It is an fMRI investigation of moral judgment/Theory of Mind, not a task requiring goal-directed problem solving, planning, or rule-based solution operations. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise/whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task-based study of problem-solving). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in 20 healthy adult participants that investigates arithmetic tasks requiring goal-directed problem solving (calculating next terms in Simple/Linear/Quad conditions), involving planning/sequencing and execution of rule-based operations (recursive arithmetic). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides voxelwise activation results with stereotactic normalization to MNI space (coordinates reported/figures/tables). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group disease comparisons only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This task-based fMRI study (healthy adults) examines inferential reasoning by exclusion, which requires subjects to infer a novel sample–comparison mapping by rejecting a trained comparison (a form of goal-directed inferential problem solving/symmetry-based reasoning). Methods report whole-brain, random-effects analyses in a healthy adult group (n=15), BOLD fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, and transformation to Talairach space; imaging contrasts (Exclusion > Baseline, S+ > Baseline) and anatomical localization are reported. The paper contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient/group-only contrasts, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving/inferential task), I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (results placed in Talairach space/stereotactic framework), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (coordinate/results reported in figures/tables as indicated).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=18 analyzed) using a computational estimation arithmetic task that requires goal-directed problem solving (selecting/evaluating and executing strategies), satisfying I5. The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (SPM, group one-sample and paired t-tests), meeting I6. Images were normalized to MNI space and ROI coordinates are provided; the text references tables/figures of voxelwise activations (indicating stereotactic results are reported), supporting I7 and I9. BOLD-sensitive EPI acquisition and BOLD analyses are described, satisfying I8. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only results, no patient-group-only contrasts, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an fMRI investigation of mental rotation (same/mirror judgments) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group SPM results in MNI/Talairach space using BOLD contrast; however, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning, sequencing, evaluating and executing operations within a rule set). Mental rotation is a visuospatial transformation task rather than a multi-step problem-solving paradigm, so inclusion criterion I5 is not met. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is a probabilistic reinforcement-learning/reward-selection paradigm focused on reward processing, prediction error, and value attribution, not on problem-solving processes such as goal evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions to derive a previously unknown correct solution within an explicit rule-based domain (semantic, algebraic, logical, etc.). It does, however, satisfy several other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants (controls) are reported (I6), BOLD fMRI analyses are used (I8), and the main text indicates voxelwise/cluster results are presented (I9). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails to meet I5 (task content).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. The experimental tasks involved passive observation of toolmaking videos with instructions to ‘imagine’ continuing the action or to ‘evaluate’ success, rather than requiring participants to perform explicit problem-solving (i.e., generate/plan and execute solutions to a presented problem under a rule set). The study does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it is excluded due to failure to satisfy I5.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. The participant sample comprises adolescents (ages 12–18), including clinical (autism) and sibling groups, not healthy adults — therefore I6 (healthy adult group-level effects) is not met. The task (Embedded Figures Task) is a perceptual visual search/shape-detection paradigm and does not clearly meet the review’s defined construct of multi-domain problem solving involving planning/sequencing/executing operations to reach a goal — therefore I5 is not met. The full text is complete and reports whole-brain BOLD analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and figures/tables, so I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are specifically triggered by the content. Given the age group and task mismatch to the meta-analysis objective, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of matrix problem solving (Raven-like) in 34 healthy adult participants. The task meets the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed matrix reasoning with rule-based operations and correct-response selection). The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected) and provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) and tables/figures of activations. BOLD fMRI is the imaging modality. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions) is present and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of propositional analogical reasoning (a fluid reasoning/problem-solving task) that includes healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain analyses. The manuscript presents voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and multiple regression results with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., left RLPFC at −27, 50, 0; right RLPFC at 27, 45, 16), and uses BOLD fMRI. Results are reported across whole-brain maps and ROI follow-ups; they are not limited to ROI-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that uses goal-directed rule-discovery and analogy tasks requiring generation of structured representations and mapping to select correct targets — processes consistent with problem solving as defined (identifying rules, planning/performing rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, presents stereotactic MNI coordinates for activation peaks, and BOLD-based analyses. Voxelwise results and ROI checks are described in the main text. No exclusion criteria apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

Exclusion E5 applies: the paper only reports between-group contrasts (higher vs lower mathematical competence) as the primary whole-brain results and does not report whole-group (task > baseline) healthy adult task effects. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task involves goal-directed problem evaluation and arithmetic operations), I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a virtual-maze navigation task that requires a goal (find way out) and planning/sequencing of actions to reach it, meeting the review's problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level (random-effects) analyses in 24 healthy adults, stereotactic coordinates (Talairach), and BOLD fMRI results presented in tables/figures. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical data reported). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adult participants examining arithmetic tasks (serial subtraction and multiplication recitation). It includes group-level whole-brain SPM analyses and reports rCBF task-related increases and activation maps (Brodmann areas). However, the supplied full text does not provide stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations in the text or tables; only Brodmann areas and referenced figures are reported. Inclusion criterion I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates) is therefore not met based on the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Hence the study must be excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I7).

This is a behavioral lesion study of moral judgment (bvFTD and prefrontal lesion patients) using written scenarios and behavioral ratings. It is not a task-based fMRI or PET study of problem solving in healthy adults. It does not report any whole-brain, group-level neuroimaging analyses in healthy adults, stereotactic coordinates, or BOLD/rCBF results. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 (not a problem-solving task), I6 (no whole-brain group-level imaging in healthy adults), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates), and I8 (no BOLD or rCBF analyses). Inclusion criteria met: none. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the paper does not provide any healthy-group task-related neuroimaging effects required by the review). Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based whole-brain fMRI investigation in healthy adult physicians/residents performing clinical reasoning MCQs that require goal-directed problem solving (diagnosis). It reports group-level, voxelwise BOLD analyses with stereotactic Talairach coordinates and provides coordinate results in tables/figures. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I5: it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined. The experimental tasks are perceptual spatial judgments (allocentric vs. egocentric left/right decisions and luminance discrimination) rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning, sequencing, or executing operations to discover a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults performing arithmetic (addition and subtraction) presented auditorily. The tasks require goal-directed calculation and execution of operations to arrive at a correct answer (problem-solving). The paper reports whole-brain group random-effects analyses, provides voxelwise results and coordinates referenced to MNI space, and uses BOLD fMRI. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for problem-solving tasks, whole-brain group effects, stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD analyses.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (12 subjects) using a sequential planning/game task (Hit-N) that requires goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions under rules (move 1–3 or 1–4 positions), and execution to reach a target — meeting the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses (event-related rfxGLM) in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic results in Talairach space and provides coordinate figures/maps (I7, I9), and reports task-related BOLD effects (I8). Analyses include whole-brain contrasts (not ROI-only) with voxelwise results and statistical maps (FDR q<0.05 and uncorrected thresholds), with methods and preprocessing described. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures), so inclusion is appropriate.

This is a task-based fMRI study of problem solving (Tower of London) in healthy adult participants (n=22). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with cluster-level correction across the whole brain, provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach space) and BOLD-related results, and includes voxelwise results in figures/tables. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study of social vs simple truth-telling (evaluative yes/no judgments about others), not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a correct or novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results described and reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm involving goal-setting, planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED because it does not meet I5.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract provided). Inclusion criteria met based on abstract: I5 (task-based fMRI of a matrix/fluid reasoning problem-solving task) and I8 (reports BOLD signal results). Inclusion criteria that cannot be confirmed due to missing full text: I6 (unclear if sample is healthy adults and that at least one whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults is reported despite mention of mixed-effects), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported in the abstract), and I9 (cannot verify voxelwise coordinate tables/figures/supplementary). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the abstract. Because key inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I9) cannot be verified and the full text is incomplete, I exclude the study pending full-text availability.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of algebraic equation solving in (presumably) healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD analyses, satisfying inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I7 (Talairach coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise/results presented in main text/figures). However, the analysis is based on a set of predefined regions-of-interest (small cubic ROIs mapped to ACT-R modules) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise/group-level analysis; therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results) and does not satisfy I6 (at least one whole-brain group-level analysis). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of linear-order (transitive) reasoning—a problem-solving/relational-inference task meeting the review’s problem-solving definition.
